items.title: The forgetful functor from Pt(Broken) to Top is a topological stack
items.statement_scope: Whole Proposition 2.3.11: the forgetful functor rho: Pt(Broken)->Top is a topological stack in the sense of Definition 2.3.3.

items.difficulty_reason: author-work-bearing-core-v1-20261114: H2 because Proposition 2.3.11 at author PDF p.13 verifies that the paper's global moduli construction Pt(Broken) is a topological stack, combining fibration-in-groupoids (Definition 2.3.1) with pullback and local-descent facts (Remarks 2.1.5 and 2.1.8) to obtain descent for the groupoid-valued functor; its difficulty lies in the global stack construction rather than a routine qualifying-exam computation.

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: Identification of Pt(Broken) as a topological stack via fibration-in-groupoids and descent from local families.

semantic_comparisons.basis: Classifies Nijenhuis operators on 2D pre-Lie algebras. No topological stack, S-family of broken lines or descent-for-groupoids conclusion.
Countable separation property for associative algebras under annihilator hypotheses E-CSP. Different hypotheses and conclusion.
Unitary Drinfeld centers and factorization homology, with canonical actions on Vect(C)/Hilb(C). Adjacent categorical language only; not the topological-stack property of Pt(Broken).
R-equivalence of automorphism groups and a radical criterion J^2=0. Different object class and conclusion.
Splitting operations for Hom-diassociative and Hom-triassociative algebras. Different algebraic structures and conclusion.
Hilbert series for dihedral invariants of a free associative algebra. Different conclusion.
Cyclic invariants of the free associative algebra and free generators. Different conclusion.
Globalization of partial group actions and an adjunction between covariant and dilated representations. Categorical but no topological stack or broken-line family.
Classification of maximal left ideals of near-trinions. Different classification problem.
Universal derivation for cyclic associative algebras. Different object class and conclusion.
Embedding non-associative algebras into associative algebras via a derivation. Different construction and conclusion.
